slides.reasoning: Design A delivers the brief's condensed-numeral futurist tone with a dramatic filled rising curve, hierarchical $4.8M hero and clean metric rule system, while Design B uses generic sans typography, stray non-palette blue/red dot fills, and a large empty right quadrant.

Design A builds a genuine illustrated hand-drawn route with layered clay/marigold/aubergine accents and a well-anchored quote bar, whereas Design B is a plain three-dot linear timeline with a large dead band of whitespace and centered text that reads as default template.

Design A's sharp before/after panels, precise rules and single dominant $780k figure are crisply aligned, while Design B's floating circles with crossing leader lines, awkward staggered boxes and mid-slide voids feel unresolved.

Design A pairs an elegant labelled allocation wheel with a restrained gold-and-mineral serif hierarchy and a well-balanced returns footer; Design B leaves large empty regions, duplicates percentages in both the ring and legend, and lets the wheel float without labels.

Design B achieves the cinematic keynote reveal with a dramatic dark product close-up and clean signal-red accents, while Design A's small centered boxed render on flat silver reads brochure-like with right-aligned captions and awkward callout rules.

Design A delivers a coherent monospaced data system, one strong performance curve with variance markers and a clearly emphasized activation gap; Design B's misleading downward slope chart and colliding 'ACTIVATION / TARGET 75%' labels are structurally broken.

Design A's transit-line diagram with terminus caps, station nodes and a charcoal north-star bar is genuinely wayfinding-authentic, whereas Design B's four bar-charts plus a black 'North Star' circle introduces an off-palette orange and leaves unbalanced right-side voids.

Design A's swimlane roadmap with week scale, citron gate diamonds and rollout ramp is dynamic and information-rich despite slight gate-label crowding, while Design B is essentially four flat rectangles—precisely the card grid the brief warned against.

Design A renders a bold circular facilitation loop with marker-style annotation and generous type, though its doubled quotation marks are a flaw; Design B's zig-zag circle chain crowds tiny text inside discs and leaves a large empty lower band with an orphaned 'Practice rule' rule.

Design A creates a memorable 68% via oversized numeral plus dot matrix and an explicit three-app fragmented journey with a full-width implication bar, while Design B's donut swallows the number in a plain ring and its footer text sits loose and unstructured.

Design A's saturated cobalt field, cyan outline title and disciplined visible/hidden UI framing feel intentionally theatrical, whereas Design B's generic audience photo, banner-strip header and boxed diagram with ragged right-aligned text weaken the keynote moment.

Design A's orange/ink split with a boxed 1.8M hero, rule-divided metrics and powder-blue priority list is confident and cohesive, while Design B scatters figures across an orange field with a large empty lower-left area and unaligned label offsets.

Design A integrates aerial photography with a purpose-built corridor map, funding progress bar and field-log annotation in a coherent journal system, whereas Design B overlays disconnected diagonal ochre bars on the photo that read as errant strokes rather than a corridor.

Design A's large letterform with accurate dot-anchored callouts, blue baseline/x-height rules and Bauhaus footer is genuinely instructional, while Design B's leader lines float disconnected from the glyph and its labels sit ambiguously against a generic ruled grid.

Design B's full-bleed culinary image and clean plum column create an editorial audience composition, whereas Design A suffers letter-spacing artifacts in its partnership-moment tags ('FUT URE T ABLE ST AGE') and a large empty right-hand void.
